watch_items.item: Workplace Relations Legislation Amendment (Building Cooperative Workplaces No. 1) Act 2026 (No. 62)
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Assent 6 Jul 2026, effect 7 Jul 2026: FWC process reforms (general protections and unlawful termination disputes without a threshold dismissal finding, on-the-papers determinations by consent, dismissal of vexatious applications and repeat-applicant bars, delegated certificates), road transport contractor rights, Commonwealth procurement preferencing, supported and intractable bargaining changes. watch_items.status_at_snapshot: AWR 2026 decided [2026] FWCFB 3500 on 2 Jun 2026 (award minimum wages +4.75%; National Minimum Wage $1,004.90 per week from 1 Jul 2026; high income threshold $190,100 and compensation cap $95,050 from 1 Jul 2026). watch_items.status_at_review: No change. The Annual Wage Review 2026 decision ([2026] FWCFB 3500, 2 June 2026) increased modern award minimum wages by 4.75% and set the National Minimum Wage at $1,004.90 per week ($26.44 per hour) from 1 July 2026. The Commission's benchbook pages give the high income threshold as $190,100 and the unfair dismissal compensation cap as $95,050 from 1 July 2026

watch_items.item: Working from home term in the Clerks - Private Sector Award 2020 (AM2024/34)
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Not on the register at the 26 August 2026 snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: Any FWC dispute decisions under the award dispute clause on clause 5A requests; any extension of a working from home term to other awards
watch_items.status_at_review: In force: the Full Bench decision [2026] FWCFB 281 (19 Oct 2026, AM2024/34) and determination PR815538 insert clause 5A 'Requests for working from home arrangements' into the Clerks - Private Sector Award 2020. The determination 'comes into operation on 26 October 2026' and takes effect for each employee from the first full pay period starting on or after that date. A request must be in writing and specify the days or pattern of days; the parties may agree to modify specified award terms; agreement must be free of coercion or duress; disputes may go to the award dispute clause. The clause sets no response time, reasons requirement or refusal grounds (the Full Bench did not adopt a union right-to-request model). Section 65 flexible working requests remain available to eligible employees
watch_items.review_basis: Decision and determination PDFs on fwc.gov.au and the Fair Work Ombudsman page (updated 26 Oct 2026) read on 2026-11-02. Clause-content detail beyond the operative date rests on secondary sources; read clause 5A before quoting it
